sources.note: For Gmbwaga (= Ngbaka-Ma'bo, CAR bank; grammar shared with Gbanziri and Monzombo): 'L'accent tonique consiste dans un coup de voix sans elevation sensible du ton.. Il se trouve ordinairement sur la premiere syllabe non affectee du signe de brievete' (stress ordinarily on the first non-short syllable), distinguished from 'accent de hauteur' (pitch). Kin variety, not Gilima; already the ngba1284 record's source.

Part 2: 'Les langues banda, ngbaka mabo et furu dans les Zones de Bosobolo et de Libenge', sec. 2.3 'Le peuple ngbaka mabo y compris gbanziri, gilima, monzombo, kpala et yango' (pp. 34-37).

sources.note: No phonology content for Gilima: the section gives 1983 census figures, lexicostatistic percentages (tables 9-10), intelligibility test results (Ngbaka Mabo understood at 95-100% in Bavula), sociolinguistic testimony (shift from Mbanza and Ngbaka to Gilima among under-35s; Gilima the only language of worship), clan history after Maes 1983, and a recommendation for Bible translation in Gilima. Sec. 1.3 explains phonetic symbols; the only remark on tone in the whole report is in Part 1 (Bantu riverine lects): 'Sauf les differences de ton, que nous n'avons pas mesurees'. Wordlists are not reprod…
